title: JuryProbe: An Empirical Consensus-Risk Diagnostic for Routing Reference-Free Factuality Judge Panels to Grounded Verification
summary: JuryProbe tests whether agreement among reference-free factuality judges hides shared errors, then uses calibration evidence to decide when accepted claims need grounded verification.
contributions: A labeled calibration probe measures correlated missed corruptions and excess unanimous false acceptance. When panel-level risk is flagged, every reference-free majority acceptance is rechecked by the same judges with references.
On Number and Entity corruptions, false-negative correlations over all corrupted claims were 0.402 and 0.368. False-consensus lifts on GPT-4o-detectable subsets were 3.13× and 18.13×, respectively.

All 34 flagged splits matched the Ground-All-Accepts policy. On a constructed negative control, stand-down avoided reference acquisition for about 28% of deployment claims, with a 0.004 absolute false-accept-rate increase versus Ground-All-Accepts.
limitations: The diagnostic offers no formal risk guarantee and does not establish reliable stand-down for natural panels.
Trusted-reference experiments are best-case diagnostics. Weak retrieval reduces true-accept coverage, and distribution shifts require recalibration.

title: ModularSQL: A Runtime Guardrail for the Multiplicity Blind Spot in Text-to-SQL
summary: ModularSQL checks executed SQL results for multiplicity problems that set-collapsing evaluation can miss. It combines a duplicate-preserving metric with selective runtime intervention.
contributions: Multiset-EX retains duplicate counts while ignoring row order. A post-selection detector triggers deterministic DISTINCT patches or candidate-based LLM rescue.
Across three released DeepEye-SQL backbones, Set-EX exceeded Multiset-EX by 5.81–6.79 percentage points on 1,532 executable BIRD-Dev queries.

The Qwen3-Coder reproduction improved Multiset-EX from 65.86% to 67.75%, preserving 72.06% Set-EX. It flagged 77 anomalies, with $0.0076 total additional LLM cost and 120 ms amortized overhead per query.
limitations: Experiments cover BIRD-Dev with SQLite. Full candidate-based rescue was tested only with the DeepEye-SQL reproduction; candidate-free components transferred to two other released prediction sets.
Deterministic patches address DISTINCT changes, not general aggregation or join repair. No additional full repair-round comparison was performed.

title: When Does Dynamic Ensembling Pay Off? Diagnosing Regionwise Gains in Regression under Distribution Shift
summary: This study asks when a small labeled target-domain probe can identify useful regional reweighting of a frozen regression-model pool under distribution shift.
contributions: D_CF5 cross-fits the risk difference between regional and global convex blends. A separate Probe-Validated Ensemble Selector compares candidates against a static-convex floor using held-out validation; the selector does not use D_CF5 as an input.
The diagnostic correlated with realized regional gains at Spearman +0.98 across 12 dataset-shift pairs and +0.83 in a 16-pair sensitivity analysis.
The prospective selector matched or improved its static floor in all 12 runs. Two deployments reduced test risk by 11% and 16%.
limitations: The diagnostic targets regional convex reweighting, not every dynamic adaptation mechanism. It requires labeled target observations.
The gate uses asymptotic validation, not a finite-sample guarantee. Evidence primarily concerns tabular regression with frozen source models and within-project preregistration.
